environment: User’s M3, visible inline Chromium 157; WebGL ANGLE Metal Renderer Apple M3; WebGPU Apple / metal-3, fallback false; luma 10.0.0-alpha.15
question: Can WebGPU preserve per-point targets, strengths and live updates at useful cost?
method: Unchanged production GLSL, corrected WebGPU arithmetic and independent raw-channel CPU reference.
conclusion: Per-point attractors preserve the tested behavior through 8,192 points, including live target changes and disabling/re-enabling. The corrected WebGPU candidate costs more than WebGL in these isolated force timings.

checks.name: Backend versus CPU
checks.detail: 72/72 checkpoint/update rows per backend. Forces, integration and independent trajectories pass; all nine disabled-stage checks per backend preserve positions exactly.

checks.name: WebGPU versus WebGL
checks.detail: 18/18 shared-input comparisons; 18/18 post-timing force/position checks also pass.

checks.name: Force-only GPU cost
checks.detail: At 8,192 points: WebGPU medians 0.324–0.487 ms versus WebGL 0.032–0.036 ms. Includes corrected arithmetic; excludes integration/drawing/uploads/readbacks.

limits: One native session, 30 fixed-alpha ticks and four checkpoints per input. No full-frame acceptance, long cooling/reheating, combined-force ordering, production setters/transitions or broader device coverage. Historical pilot picking and color failures remain open.
visual: Live positions evolve separately; this preview is not recorded evidence.
